chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from one of his companions, from Aban, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

O group of the Shia, the Shia of the Progeny of Muhammad! Be the 'Numruqah al-Wusta' (the central/intermediate group). The exaggerator (Al-Ghali) will return to you, and the follower (Al-Tali) will join you. A man from the Ansar, called Sa'd, said to him, 'May I be your ransom, what is the exaggerator?' He said, 'A people who say about us what we do not say about ourselves. So those are not from us, and we are not from them.' He said, 'So what is the follower?' He said, 'The scout who seeks goodness; goodness reaches him, and he is rewarded for it.' Then he turned to us and said, 'By Allah, there is no exemption (from accountability) with us from Allah, nor is there between us and Allah a kinship (that grants automatic favor), nor is there an argument for us against Allah, nor do we draw near to Allah except through obedience. So whoever among you is obedient to Allah, our Wilayah will benefit him; and whoever among you is disobedient to Allah, our Wilayah will not benefit him. Woe to you! Do not be deceived. Woe to you! Do not be deceived.'

key_terms.التَّالِي: The follower (one who follows the path of goodness)
key_terms.النُّمْرُقَةَ الْوُسْطَى: The central/intermediate group (a metaphor for balance)
key_terms.الْغَالِي: The exaggerator (one who overstates the status of the Imams)
key_terms.الْمُرْتَادُ: The scout/seeker (one who actively seeks good)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the exaggerator and the follower in Shia theology according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the 'middle path' (al-nimruqah al-wusqa) as the ideal state for Shia, avoiding both the exaggeration of the Ghaliyyah who attribute divine qualities to the Imams and the negligence of the Taliyyah. He clarifies that Wilayah is not an automatic shield but a means of grace contingent upon obedience to Allah, warning that disobedience nullifies the benefit of association with the Imams. This hadith underscores the Shia theological principle that spiritual proximity to the Ahl al-Bayt is inextricably linked to personal piety and adherence to divine commandments.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from one of his companions, from Aban, from Amro Bin Khalid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘O group of Shia, the Shia of the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>! Take a central position. The exaggerator would return to you and the ‘Ta’aly’ would catch up with you’. So a man from the Helpers called Sa’ad, said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! What is the exaggerator?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘People who are saying regarding us<sup>asws</sup> (that which) we<sup>asws</sup> are not saying regarding ourselves<sup>asws</sup>. So those are not from us<sup>asws</sup> and we<sup>asws</sup> are not from them’. He said, ‘So what is the ‘Ta’aly’?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The apostate indenting the goodness. The goodness reaches him and he is Recompensed upon it’.
Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> turned to face us and he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘By Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>! There is no freedom (from the Fire) with us<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> from Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, nor is there between us<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> and Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> a relationship, nor is there an argument for us<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> against Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, nor do we<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> get closer to Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> except by obedience. So the one from you who was obedient to Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, our<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> Wilayah would benefit him, and the one from you who was disobedient to Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, our<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> Wilayah would not benefit him. Woe be unto you! Do not be decieved. Woe be unto you! Do not be deceived’.
en.sarwar: 6. Hamid ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama’a from certain individuals of his people from Aban from ‘Amr ibn Khalid from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘O the community of Shi’a, Shi’a of Muhammad (a.s.) be the central support so that both al- Ghali and al-Tali refer to you.’ A man from Ansar (people of Madina) called Sa’d, said, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, what is the meaning of al-GhaliV The Imam said, ‘They are the people who say about us what we do not say about ourselves. Thus, they are not of our people and we are not of their people.’ The man then asked, ‘Who are al-TaliV The Imam said, ‘They are those who search for good. They receive good instructions (from our Shi’a) and are rewarded for it.’ The Imam then turned to us and said, ‘I swear by Allah that we do not possess any amnesty from Allah and there is no family relation between Allah and us nor do we possess any authority over Allah. We do not seek nearness to Allah through any other means but obedience to Him. Whoever of you is obedient to Allah it (our guardianship, Wilayah ) will benefit him, and whoever of you is disobedient to Allah our guardianship, Wilayah, will not benefit him. What is the matter with you? Do not be misled! What is the matter with you? Do not be misled!”’
